scenes.spoken_text: Living-space planning starts with people and activities. Compare conversation and viewing arrangements, testing circulation and access against explicit acceptance points.
scenes.caption: Living-space planning starts with people and activities. Compare conversation and viewing arrangements, testing circulation and access against explicit acceptance points.

scenes.spoken_text: Record everyday and guest occupancy and priorities for conversation, viewing or reading. Conversation needs reciprocal sightlines; viewing needs a suitable orientation to the screen from the intended seats. Seat count alone does not establish usability. Draw sightlines and identify seats requiring an awkward turn for the requested activity; do not derive seating comfort from screen size.
scenes.caption: Judge sightlines against the intended activity.

scenes.spoken_text: Map routes from the entrance to destinations, including open doors, moved chairs and table use. Where the brief allows, keep through-traffic outside the conversation group. Measure the narrowest point in realistic operating states and compare it with documented user and project requirements. A clearance copied from an image is not a universal rule or evidence of accessibility compliance.
scenes.caption: Measure bottlenecks in occupied and opening states.

scenes.display_title: Compare layouts using the same acceptance points
scenes.spoken_text: Keep room boundaries and assumed occupancy fixed when comparing A for conversation with B for viewing. Assess sightlines, through-routes, door opening and table access using the same criteria. Record trade-offs rather than changing drawing scale to flatter a proposal. Floor markings and a simple use mock-up can test positions before selection; symmetry alone is not a functional pass.
scenes.caption: Use common criteria and state the trade-off.

scenes.spoken_text: The family prioritises conversation and daily balcony access. A faces seats toward each other but places a chair in the balcony route. B moves the chair to the side while retaining visual connection. Prefer B subject to checking the narrowest route and balcony door operation on site; an extra seat must not reintroduce the conflict. Decision: prefer B subject to route and door verification.
scenes.caption: Decision: prefer B subject to route and door verification.

scenes.display_title: Submit two same-scale layouts with activities, sightlines, circulation and acceptance criteria; justify the choice.
